content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore xml security audit and review within XML Security and Safe Processing. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: XML Security Audit and Review matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about inspecting parser settings, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat XML, schemas, and stylesheets from outside the trust boundary as untrusted input. Safe processing requires explicit parser and resolver policy, bounded resource use, and fail-closed configuration.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Inspecting parser settings; Reviewing external resource resolution; Dependency and parser updates; Security test cases; Documenting security assumptions; Security should be treated as a core module, not an optional afterthought. OWASP recommends; disabling DTDs where they are unnecessary, controlling external-resource resolution, and applying; resource limits to XML processing.. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: XML Security Audit and Review
content_blocks.code:
from defusedxml.ElementTree import fromstring

# Parse only a bounded, untrusted XML string with a hardened parser.
root = fromstring("<catalog><product>Notebook</product></catalog>")
print(root.tag)
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. For untrusted documents, prefer a hardened parser (for Python, review defusedxml and current Expat guidance), disable DTDs and external entity resolution unless a reviewed requirement demands them, and separately restrict network/file access used by schema or stylesheet resolution.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the sample to its exact starting state before each experiment. Change one element, attribute, expression, or constraint at a time, then compare the result with the expected behavior.
content_blocks.limitations: This defensive example requires the defusedxml package, which is not installed by this course patch. Pin and review dependencies, forbid DTDs when not needed, restrict schema/stylesheet resolvers, and enforce input/resource limits. Never run untrusted parsing in an unisolated production process.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: For untrusted XML, use reviewed secure parser settings, disable unnecessary DTD/external-resource resolution, bound resource use, and fail closed if security configuration cannot be applied. Distinguish well-formedness, schema validity, and application-level correctness; they are different checks.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small synthetic example that demonstrates “Inspecting parser settings”. Then add one boundary case involving “Reviewing external resource resolution”. Write down what should happen before testing, and record the exact output or processor message afterward.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a document is correct because it looks readable.
common_mistakes.why: Visual appearance does not prove well-formedness, schema validity, correct namespace handling, or application-level meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse and validate the document with the intended processor, then assert its meaning using a focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing specification features with processor support.
common_mistakes.why: A standard may define features that a specific runtime does not implement.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the version and feature support; test with the actual target processor.

common_mistakes.why: Missing values, wrong types, namespace differences, or boundary inputs can expose failures.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a valid case, an invalid case, and an edge case to the verification notes.
